newsitem.title: UK: Safeway gains on market share report.
newsitem.headline: Safeway gains on market share report.

text.p: Shares in Safeway Plc rose on Thursday as a report from market research group AGB showed the company increasing market share, traders and analysts said.
Safeway was up 2-1/2p at 338 while other food retail stocks were little changed, with J. Sainsbury Plc unchanged at 368-1/2, Tesco Plc unchanged at 308p and Asda Group Plc up 1/4p at 105.
Analysts said market research group AGB figures showed Safeway's market share rising to 10.4 percent in September from 10.1 percent the month before. "It seems to be on a recovery path," said one.
Compared with September last year, AGB said Safeway had picked up market share of 0.9 percentage points, according to analysts.
AGB also showed Asda increasing market share to 13.1 percent in September from 12.6 percent in August, while Sainsbury was static at 19.3 percent.
Tesco dipped to 22.7 percent from 22.9 percent but was still well ahead of its 22.0 percent share in July.
A spokeswoman for Safeway said the company was aware of the AGB figures but said it was more important to look for the long-term trend than short-term swings.
"They are obviously interesting figures," the spokeswoman said, "but by their very nature they are never entirely representative."
No-one at Asda was immediately available for comment.

Elsewhere in the sector, KwikSave Plc backtracked from yesterday's gain, driven by speculation of a merger with Iceland Plc. Both groups are seen as being squeezed by their increasingly aggressive large rivals.
KwikSave was down 10-1/2p at 319-1/2 and Iceland was down 1/2p at 89.
